findings.title: website_name leaks TL0 users' websites to anonymous viewers, bypassing untrusted attribute protection
findings.body: The `website` attribute is deliberately hidden for TL0 users viewed by anonymous visitors via `untrusted_attributes :website` (which checks `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`), an anti-spam/privacy measure so new users can't use their profile website for link spam. The new `website_name` attribute computes its value from the same `object.user_profile.website` but is not added to `untrusted_attributes` and its inclusion check (`include_website_name`, which only tests `website.present?`) never consults the scope. As a result, an anonymous viewer of a TL0 user's profile JSON now receives the website host — and the full host+path whenever the host matches the instance domain — even though `website` itself is suppressed. This defeats the restriction; `website_name` must be gated by the same `restrict_user_fields?` logic as `website`.

findings.title: include_website_name is missing the trailing '?' so ActiveModel::Serializer never calls it
findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializer's conditional-inclusion hook must be named `include_<attribute>?` (with a question mark), as used elsewhere in this file (e.g. `include_email?`, `include_stats?`). The method defined here is `include_website_name` without the `?`, so AMS never invokes it and the guard is dead code: `website_name` is serialized unconditionally, appearing as an explicit `null` in the JSON for every user without a website (and, combined with the first issue, there is no effective scope check at all). Rename the method to `include_website_name?` for the filter to take effect.
